evidence: src/infrastructure/http-server.ts: `createApp(service = new TaskManagementService())` holds all route definitions, and every route calls a service method (createUser, createProject, createTask, listProjectTasks, assignTask, markTaskDone).
src/infrastructure/http-server.ts: a single error middleware maps `DomainError` to `error.statusCode` and anything else to 500. This logic appears nowhere else.
src/infrastructure/http-server.ts: the shared helpers `body`, `stringField` and `optionalStringField` are used consistently by every route that reads a request body.
src/infrastructure/server.ts: only reads PORT and calls `createApp().listen(port, ...)`. It repeats no routing or error logic.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files deal with one thing: delivering the task API over HTTP. http-server.ts builds the Express app in `createApp`. It defines the routes, adapts requests through small helpers, and turns errors into responses. server.ts is a thin entrypoint that only calls `createApp().listen(port)`. Each rule lives in one place. Errors map to status codes in one error-handling middleware that reads `DomainError.statusCode`. The 404 response is defined once. Body parsing goes through the shared `body`, `stringField` and `optionalStringField` helpers. Every route calls `TaskManagementService` and never reaches past it into domain internals. The per-route try/catch is repeated boilerplate, but it repeats no business rule or invariant.
